requirement_summary: 02_FUNCTIONAL_REQUIREMENTS_AND_PROGRAMS.md FR-COM-004: '모든 결과는 정책 버전, 입력 Hash, 실행환경, 도구 버전, 결과 Hash를 기록한다.' FR-COM-005: '동일 입력·정책·도구 버전은 재현 가능한 판정 구조를 가져야 한다.'
subject: SemanticAssuranceV2WorkflowService.resultReproducibilityCheck via assurance.result.reproducibility-check; contracts/result-reproducibility-check.v1.schema.json (NEW)
coverage_notes: FR-COM-004 is closed structurally: the schema's own required list forces every result object to carry all 5 named identity fields (policy_version/input_hash/execution_environment/tool_version/result_hash), and the Java layer additionally requiredText()s each one, failing closed on any missing field. FR-COM-005 is closed by real cross-record computation: resultReproducibilityCheckDetectsADifferingResultHashForTheSameInputPolicyAndTool is the direct test -- two results sharing identical (input_hash, policy_version, tool_version) but producing different result_hash values are flagged as a genuine REPRODUCIBILITY_VIOLATION group naming both differing result_ids, not silently accepted. resultReproducibilityCheckNeverFlagsDifferentInputsAsAViolation proves the equivalence key is real (different input_hash means no comparison is even attempted, so no false positive). execution_environment is deliberately excluded from the equivalence key (proven by resultReproducibilityCheckIsReproducibleWhenMatchingKeysShareTheSameResultHash using two different execution_environment values that still reproduce identically) since the requirement's own wording names only 입력·정책·도구 버전 (input/policy/tool version) as the reproducibility key, not execution environment.
open_gap: Operates on a caller-supplied batch of result records; there is no live validation-execution runtime in this codebase that actually re-runs a validation under identical input/policy/tool conditions and produces a second real result_hash to compare against the first (same disclosed 'caller-supplied representation, not live system integration' pattern as every other real-computation closure this session) -- this operation can only detect a reproducibility violation if two already-produced results are submitted together in one call; it does not itself trigger or orchestrate a re-run.
